mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 0.2%) compresses equity discount rates and increases present value of future cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.2%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% in one month indicate broad consumer demand contraction, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 1 month, or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing supply contraction (INDPRO below 100.5) indicates reduced industrial output and potential recessionary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to declining corporate production and earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100.5, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points over one month signals monetary tightening, raising equity discount rates and reducing liquidity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.3pp in 1 month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% and rising unemployment (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points in one month indicate severe labor market contraction, reducing consumer spending and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines > 0.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS declines > 0.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month, or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index above 215 indicates elevated inflation, prompting potential central bank rate hikes that increase equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 215, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales above 360,000 million dollars (RSAFS > 360) indicate strong consumer spending, supporting corporate revenue growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS > 360, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.
